summary: # Smooth Curve | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and I'm going to walk you through the new updates we have to our Smooth Curve tool. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Overview of the Smooth Curve Tool Here we have some patterns, and what we're going to go through is our Smooth Curve tool. As you can see, I have some wonky curves. You could use your Curve Point tool or even your Edit Pattern tool. The Curve Point tool is shortcut V, but it's also right over here for my Edit Curve Point tool. I could, of course, just click and add a curve point and start to edit and adjust this line if I'd like to. It's totally easy and normal—just click, move, and adjust it. ## Editing Curves This is definitely one way you can do this, and it's very easy. You can also go to your Edit Pattern tool, select that, click on the edge because these have Bezier handles, and I could click and adjust it. Right-click and adjust those Bezier handles. I could also go to my Curvature tool and just click and move this curve around. All of these are great and easy ways to edit and adjust your Curve Point tool. ### Using the Smooth Curve Tool Let's go ahead and edit this. I'll just adjust this. We’re going to use the Smooth Curve tool to make all of these adjustments. The Smooth Curve tool is right down here in your 2D toolbar. You can click and use this. If you have your tools grouped, go to Settings > User Settings > User Interface, and turn on "Group Tools." If your tools are grouped, the Smooth Curve option will be inside your Edit Pattern tool. I prefer to ungroup my tools just because I like to see all my tools, but sometimes that can be overwhelming to see all the tools in close. If you like to group them, keep them grouped; that’s where you’ll find all of your editing tools. ## Traditional Methods of Using the Smooth Curve Tool There are a few original ways in which this tool can still be used today. One of the original ways is to easily click on a line or even a segment point. For example, click and hold down to adjust the curve of this line. You can also click and hold down while using your right mouse button. A pop-up will appear, allowing you to type in the numbers you want, like adjusting Line 1 and Line 2—different sides of one line. You can even move and adjust if you want the curve to go out or in. If you’re not happy with what you did, you can hit cancel. This is a traditional way to use this tool. Another original method involves creating a reference line and using that line to edit another line. To do this, click on one segment point and then click on another. This line then appears as the reference line that you will use to edit the selected line. Once you're happy with the shape, hit enter, and it will be all set. ## New Methods for Using the Smooth Curve Tool Now, let’s get into the new method. You can apply curve points or just edit curve points as well as edit the line and not just the reference line. I know that was a lot to hear at once, so don’t worry—I’ll walk you through it all. For instance, if I want to adjust a specific curve, I can click once here and then click once there to select two different segment points. Now, instead of clicking on my reference line, I will continue to work on this current line. I can just click and move this around to edit the curve. ### Adding Curve Points If I want to add some curve points, I can hold down Control and add them in. I can then click and move this line around. Holding down Control allows me to edit each curve point individually instead of adjusting the entire line. When I release Control, I can move the whole line together. Once I'm happy with all these adjustments, I can hit enter, and it will apply my changes. It will also apply to the symmetrical pattern. ## Final Adjustments Now, I see there are still some tricky parts. I can click on different areas of the line to create my reference line. Holding down Control allows me to adjust that reference line using curve points. Once satisfied, I can hit enter again, and the adjustments will be applied. If I don't like the adjustments, I can go to my Edit Pattern tool, select the segment point, right-click, and choose "Convert to Curve Point." I can quickly switch to my curve points using the shortcut key V and move them around. ### Conclusion You might be asking, "But can’t you just edit curve points using your curve tools?" Yes, but this tool gives you control over editing one section at a time. This is especially helpful because it allows for precise adjustments without affecting the entire line. As you can see, the Smooth Curve tool is powerful and really helpful for making easy edits and adjusting patterns more accurately than ever before. Thank you so much for watching! I hope you enjoyed and learned a lot. If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don’t forget to like and subscribe, and check out all of our great videos on our YouTube channel. Thanks again for watching, and keep having fun in Clo!
